questions.answerExplanation:
(a) It returns null, because nothing has been saved under 'theme' yet. The if condition is false, so the page is NOT in dark mode.
(b) Yes, the page is in dark mode. setItem saved 'dark' in localStorage, which stays in the browser even after it is closed. When the page loads, getItem returns 'dark' and the class is added.
(c) Clicking still turns the page dark, but after reloading it goes back to light. Without setItem the choice is never saved, so getItem returns null on reload.

(a) When the page loads the paragraph is empty, so no message is shown. When the button is clicked, showMessage runs and "Hello!" appears in the paragraph.
(b) "Hello!" appears straight away when the page loads, without any click. The brackets call showMessage immediately instead of passing the function to addEventListener, so it is not run when the button is clicked.
(c) The message appears when the user moves their mouse over the button, without needing to click it. The event name decides which user action runs the function.

(a) "Welcome, Sam" is shown in the paragraph. .value reads the text the user typed into the input box.
(b) The browser submits the form the normal way and reloads the page, so the welcome message disappears straight away (or is never seen). preventDefault is what stops the browser's default submit behaviour.
(c) Add the required attribute to the input: `<input id="name" type="text" required>`. The browser then stops the form from submitting and shows a message asking the user to fill in the field, so no welcome message is shown.
